report.tagline: Meta's photo and short video app, where 3 billion people share posts, Stories and Reels and message friends.
report.simpleSummary: Instagram is an app for sharing photos and short videos with friends and followers. You scroll a feed, watch Reels (short vertical videos), view Stories that vanish after 24 hours, and chat in DMs. It is free. Meta, which owns it, makes money by showing ads between posts and Reels, targeted to what each person likes.

overview.whatItDoes: Instagram lets people post photos and videos, watch content from friends, creators and brands, and message each other. Over time it has added Stories (2016), Reels (2020), Threads integration (2023) and many AI features. It is mostly a video and messaging app now, with a feed driven by recommendations.
howItWorks: Users follow friends, creators and brands, and the algorithm also recommends content they might like.
People post to the feed, share Stories for 24 hours, make Reels, and send DMs.
The algorithm ranks content using what you watch, like, share and save.
Advertisers pay Meta to show ads in feed, Stories, Reels and Explore, targeted by interests.
Creators earn through brand deals, subscriptions, gifts and bonus programmes.
overview.valueProposition: For users: stay close to friends and discover fun videos in one app. For businesses: reach almost anyone with targeted ads and shoppable posts.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Short vertical videos ranked by AI, launched in 2020 to compete with TikTok.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Biggest driver of time spent and ad growth. In India it filled the gap after TikTok was banned in 2020.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Photos and videos that disappear after 24 hours, copied from Snapchat in 2016.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Daily habit for sharing casual moments and a major ad slot.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Private chats, often for sharing Reels with friends.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Sharing in DMs is now a key signal for the algorithm and keeps friends engaged.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Shows content from accounts you do not follow.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Helps discovery and keeps the feed full.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Private by default, PG-13 style content filters, sleep mode and parental controls.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Reduces regulatory risk and builds parents' trust.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Ads in every surface, plus product tags and click-to-message ads.

businessModel.summary: Instagram makes almost all its money from ads. Every time users scroll, Meta can show a targeted ad. More users and more time spent means more ad slots, and better targeting means advertisers pay more for each one.

revenueStreams.detail: Ads between short videos, the fastest growing slot.
Ads that open a DM or WhatsApp chat with a business, big in India.
Paid verification and creator subscriptions, a small share.

businessModel.pricing: Free for users. Ads are bought in an auction; small businesses can start with a few hundred rupees.
costDrivers: Data centres and AI for recommendations
businessModel.unitEconomics: Rough estimate. Meta earns very different amounts per user by region. A US user might be worth well over $60 a year in ads across Meta apps, while an Indian user might be worth only a few dollars. If Instagram earned about $70 billion from about 3 billion users, that is roughly $23 per user per year on average. Serving a user costs much less than that, mainly servers and moderation, so each extra user is very profitable, especially in rich markets.

howTheyGetUsers: Friends inviting friends and contact syncing
Being the default social app among young people in India
whatBringsUsersBack: Notifications for likes, comments and DMs
growth.moat: Instagram has 3 billion users and the social graph of who follows whom, which is very hard to copy. Its ad system, powered by Meta's AI and data, gives advertisers better results than most rivals. And Meta has shown it can copy rivals' best features, like Stories and Reels, quickly.

competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Instagram is more social; YouTube pays creators better.

competitors.name: Snapchat
competitors.positioning: Camera and messaging app for close friends.

competitors.name: Moj and Josh (India)
competitors.positioning: Indian short video apps for regional languages.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Instagram has the bigger brand and ad system.

improvementIdeas.problem: Hacked business accounts lose income and trust.

improvementIdeas.problem: Creators move to YouTube for pay.
Many Indian users prefer Hindi, Tamil or Bengali content.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Daily active users in tier 2 and 3 cities

pmLessons: Copying can work if you add your own strength. Stories and Reels succeeded because Instagram already had the users.
In social apps, sharing is the life force, not just watching.
Safety features can be product features that build trust with parents and regulators.
Ads must be balanced against experience; too many can slowly drive users away.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you measure the success of Teen Accounts?
interviewQuestions.hint: Define goals (safety, trust), choose metrics (harmful content views, parent adoption), add guardrails (teen retention), and discuss trade-offs.

interviewQuestions.question: Instagram wants more people to post, not just watch. What would you build?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find why people do not post (fear, effort), suggest low-pressure formats, track sharing rate.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Instagram show more ads in Reels?
interviewQuestions.hint: Model revenue per extra ad against time spent loss, run A/B tests by market, use guardrails.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Instagram's north star?
interviewQuestions.hint: Daily active sharers, broken into users, sharing rate, time spent with value and ad value.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you compete with YouTube for Indian creators?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare pay, reach and tools; suggest revenue share or brand deal tools; track creator retention.
